content.comment_body: Hello, apologies for the confusion. I'm experiencing a similar issue. My device detection offers an option for [article_no] within the "slave" selection menu.

Could you please specify your problem more clearly? Simply stating "I believe I have the same issue" is not descriptive. Also, mentioning that your device detection provides an option for [article_no] under the "slave" selection means you can only assign this as a slave device in network project mode using "Add New Device." Which [product_name] version are you using?

Sorry for the repeated message. I'm using [product_name] version [version_no]. The only available selection I have appears under the "slave" menu. My main question is whether my device will work properly if chosen as a "slave." Thank you.

Sorry, but I'm not following your explanation. There isn't a "Slave" option in the hardware selection; there are only selections like [article_no] and other standard versions. You can only choose a slave role in the network project view, which is unrelated to hardware selection.
Thank you for your reply. I've attached a screenshot for reference regarding my question.

I understand what you mean by "Slave" device in this context. As I've mentioned earlier, this selection is only available in a network project within the network view. This relates to device communication configuration, not hardware selection. There are two main ways for these devices to communicate: 1) Master/Slave: One device (master) runs the program and accesses peripherals on the other device (slave), which only shares its I/O. 2) Master/Master: Each device has its own program but can also access I/O on the other device via the network.

analysis.insight_summary: The primary concern discussed involves ambiguity in software menus regarding the device selection and assigning roles such as 'slave' for [product_name] identified by [article_no]. The confusion is whether selecting a device as 'slave' affects hardware behavior or only applies to network communication settings. Contributors clarified that 'slave' refers strictly to network configuration and is not tied to the actual hardware selection, pointing out that the user interface or documentation should more clearly differentiate these aspects.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to clearly distinguish between hardware selection and communication setup, with transparent menus and documentation to ensure devices operate as intended after configuration.
